headline: The inline-style control isolates next-yak's wrapper tax: with the value written straight to `style` and folding on, `next-yak-9.7` ties `vanilla` (0.629 vs 0.615 ms/1k), and the 9.6.0 baseline without the perf runtime is 2.2× slower.

microbench.why: With the dynamic value written directly to the `style` attribute and the class fully static, the styled perf runtime folds `<Box>` to a plain `<div>` and renders at 0.629 ms/1k, within 2% of `vanilla` (0.615). The diagnostic twins show the two levers: `next-yak-9.7-nofold` (0.918 ms/1k) is the returned `Yak` wrapper with folding off, and the 9.6.0 baseline `next-yak` (1.36) is the same wrapper without the perf runtime, 2.2× the folded path.

autocannon.why: Under load the folded inline-style path serves 1189 req/s against `vanilla`'s 1220. Folding off drops it to 909 (`next-yak-9.7-nofold`) and the 9.6.0 baseline to 625, the wrapper tax made visible per request.

attribution.why: The folded path renders in 0.750 ms with a 0.124 ms library slice, just over `vanilla` (0.695). Turning folding off doubles the library slice to 0.197 ms (1.09 ms total) and the 9.6.0 baseline to 0.489 ms (1.54 ms), each an extra `Yak` render per element.

hydrate.why: The folded path hydrates with `vanilla` at 49.3-49.8 ms; the returned wrapper adds a little (`next-yak-9.7-nofold` 51.7 ms, 9.6.0 baseline 54.7).

inp.why: Re-rendering one element with a fresh inline value is a ~7.20-7.70 ms tie between the folded path and `vanilla`; the wrapper adds nothing measurable on the interaction.

mount.why: Cold mount ties at 64.7-65.1 ms for the folded path and `vanilla`; folding off adds a few ms (`next-yak-9.7-nofold` 68.6, 9.6.0 baseline 74.2).

renderTiming.why: One recalc for both lanes; an inline style changes the value, not the recalc count.

payload.why: `vanilla` ships 5.50 kB gzipped; the folded next-yak path adds its small runtime at 6.51 kB. Folding off and the 9.6.0 baseline barely change it (6.71 and 6.52 kB); the cost here is CPU, not bytes.

nsweep.why: Scaling to 4000 elements, the folded path holds 2.79 ms with `vanilla` (2.72). Folding off rises to 4.12 ms and the 9.6.0 baseline to 6.20 ms as the `Yak` wrapper renders per element.

crossCase: `dyn-inline` closes the dynamic trio (`dyn-translate` the naive version, `dyn-fair` the hand-optimized one, both above). It carries only the next-yak family and `vanilla` because it is the reference floor for a value that never needs a class at all. Folded, `next-yak-9.7` ties `vanilla`; this is where the perf runtime's worth over 9.6.0 is starkest (0.629 vs 1.36 ms/1k) with no styling to hide behind.
